scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I'm 33 years old and have been living with my parents most of my life. They charge me $200, which is pretty reasonable where we live, and I don't have to deal with finding a new place, which is a big plus. We mostly get along, but I tend to avoid them a lot. Recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of that, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to get up and help bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute. Honestly, I was too into the game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I told him I'd do it in a minute. He said that "in a minute" was now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. That led to a huge shouting match, and now they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They have their "golden child," and it's frustrating when they throw his achievements in my face. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but since I pay rent, I feel like I have the right to say no when they ask for help with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole here? Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things. First, the dynamics of living with parents as an adult. It's not uncommon, but it does come with its own set of challenges. Paying rent is one thing, but living under the same roof means there are shared responsibilities and expectations. When my mom asked me to help with groceries, I was playing a game. I told her I'd do it in a minute, but I didn't follow through. My dad got frustrated and took the controller, leading to an argument. Now, they're threatening to leave and expecting me to find a place by Friday, which is unrealistic. I also feel resentful about the comparison to my younger brother, who is seen as the golden child. That adds to the tension. On the other hand, I do pay rent, which gives me some financial independence, but living with parents often means there are still expectations about contributing to the household. So, am I the asshole? Well, I didn't help when asked, which led to an argument. But I also feel like I have the right to say no because I pay rent. However, living in a shared space means there are shared responsibilities. Maybe I should have been more considerate of their needs, especially since the remodel has made it harder to avoid each other. Also, the comparison to my brother adds emotional weight to the situation. It's not fair to bring that up during an argument, but I can see why they might feel that way. In the end, both sides have valid points. I need to communicate better and perhaps find a middle ground where I can contribute to the household without feeling like I'm being treated unfairly. It's a tough spot to be in, but acknowledging both perspectives might help resolve the conflict.
